people.label: Older people
missingFacts: whether they live alone (NI Lone Pensioner Allowance, single person discount)
whether they have a private or workplace pension pot (Pension Wise, lost pensions)

people.label: Disabled people and people with a long-term health condition
missingFacts: whether the home needs adapting (Disabled Facilities Grant)
whether a disabled person needs an extra room or wheelchair space (Council Tax disabled band reduction)
whether a child in the home is disabled (DLA for children, Child Disability Payment, Family Fund)
whether the condition was caused by work (Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit)
whether they need help to get or keep a job because of the condition (Access to Work)

people.label: Unpaid carers
missingFacts: whether the carer is in education (Young Carer Grant)
whether the person cared for gets a disability benefit

people.label: Families with children and people expecting a baby
missingFacts: number of children and each child's age band
school stage of each child (primary, secondary, 16 to 19)
distance to the nearest suitable school (school transport)
whether they use or need childcare
whether they are bringing up someone else's child after a parent died (Guardian's Allowance)

people.label: Young people (16 to 24)
missingFacts: whether they are in school, college or training
whether they are a care leaver
whether they live without parental support

people.label: People out of work or about to lose work
missingFacts: whether they were made redundant and how long they worked there (statutory redundancy pay)
whether the employer has gone bust (Redundancy Payments Service)
how long they have been on benefits (Budgeting Loan, Job Start Payment)

people.label: People in low-paid work
missingFacts: whether they pay for work items themselves (tax relief for job expenses)
whether they are married or in a civil partnership and who earns less (Marriage Allowance)
whether they think they were paid less than the minimum wage

people.label: People going through a life event
missingFacts: recent job loss or redundancy
separation or divorce
being a victim of violent crime (criminal injuries compensation)
a home emergency such as fire or flood (crisis grants)
a recent death with no will or known family (bona vacantia)

people.label: People who moved to the UK
missingFacts: whether they can get public funds, asked only as yes, no or unsure, never the visa type (most benefits are closed to people with no recourse to public funds; many charity, school and NHS help still applies)

people.label: People helping someone else (family, advisers, support workers)
missingFacts: a 'checking for someone else' mode that changes the 'you' voice
whether the person helped agrees to the check

people.label: Self-employed and sole traders
missingFacts: trading income band and how long they have traded
whether they pay Class 2 or Class 4 National Insurance

people.label: Small firms
missingFacts: sector, size, nation and council area of the business
rateable value band (business rates relief)

people.label: Community groups and small charities
missingFacts: legal form and charity number if any
area of work and annual income band

people.label: Employers checking support for staff
missingFacts: number of staff and payroll size band
whether they take on apprentices or disabled staff

people.label: Landlords
missingFacts: property type, EPC band and council area
whether tenants get housing support

people.label: UK people living abroad
missingFacts: country of residence
years of UK National Insurance record

missingFacts: area-level answers only, never personal ones

connectors.name: GOV.UK Content API
connectors.covers: The structured JSON behind any GOV.UK page: GET https://www.gov.uk/api/content/<path>. Gives body text, parts, updated dates and links for every central scheme page.
connectors.notes: No key. Max 10 requests a second per client. Content under the Open Government Licence v3.0. The API is in beta and may change. Checked 2026-11-04.

connectors.name: GOV.UK Search API
connectors.covers: Finds GOV.UK pages by filters such as content_store_document_type, mainstream_browse_pages and organisations, with aggregates. Use it to list every benefit, grant and 'answer' page to diff against the packs.
connectors.notes: No key. Endpoint answered on 2026-11-04 (769 documents of type 'answer'). Filter names change over time, so read the live response rather than hard-coding counts.

connectors.name: GOV.UK benefits calculators page
connectors.covers: Names the government-endorsed independent calculators (entitledto, Turn2us, Policy in Practice) and the groups they do not serve well.
connectors.notes: Comparator list only. Checked 2026-11-04.

connectors.name: entitledto
connectors.covers: Comparator: public benefits calculator and a paid adviser calculator. Use to sanity-check Beacon results by hand, not as a data source.
connectors.notes: The homepage does not mention an API or reuse terms. Any automated use needs a commercial agreement.

connectors.name: Policy in Practice Better Off Calculator
connectors.covers: Comparator: Better Off Calculator, plus LIFT analytics that councils license to find residents missing support.
connectors.notes: Free for individuals. Council licensing terms are not published; contact the company. Not a source for Beacon rules.

connectors.name: Turn2us benefits calculator
connectors.covers: Comparator: benefits calculator that organisations can embed.
connectors.notes: Site terms limit use to personal, non-commercial purposes; anything else needs written permission from Turn2us.

connectors.name: GOV.UK local-authority API

connectors.name: GOV.UK local transactions (Local Links Manager via Content API)
connectors.covers: GOV.UK 'local transaction' pages carry an LGSL service code; GOV.UK maps each code to the right page on every council's website. This is the fastest way to get a per-council link for services like Council Tax Reduction, Blue Badge and bus passes.

connectors.name: postcodes.io
connectors.covers: Postcode to admin_district and its ONS code (for example Brent, E09000005), country, ward, parish, LSOA and deprivation index. Already used by Beacon for nation.

connectors.name: ONS Open Geography Portal

strategy.why: Council Tax discounts and disregards (single person, disabled band, severe mental impairment) need only one or two new facts and apply in every council in England, Scotland and Wales.
strategy.schemesEstimate: 3 national rules, linked per council (317 in England alone)
strategy.connector: GOV.UK local-authority API + LGSL local transaction links

strategy.why: Free school meals in all four nations, school transport and bursaries reuse facts Beacon already asks (child, benefits, income); England's 2026 to 2027 change makes every Universal Credit family qualify.
strategy.connector: GOV.UK Content API, mygov.scot, gov.wales, nidirect

strategy.why: Scotland has the biggest gap: Scottish Child Payment, Best Start, Child Winter Heating, Young Carer Grant and the Scottish Welfare Fund are well defined and reuse existing facts.
Marriage Allowance, job expenses relief, Carer's Credit, Help to Save and Budgeting Loans are UK-wide and need small new facts; GOV.UK Content API already powers the reader.
Lost pensions, Child Trust Funds, dormant accounts and tax refunds are pure 'money already yours' and Beacon only needs to link out, so no sensitive data is collected.
strategy.connector: Pension Tracing Service, HMRC CTF tool, My Lost Account, NS&I (link out only)

strategy.why: Water social tariffs and WaterSure exist at every water company; broadband social tariffs are already one live scheme that can be split per provider from Ofcom's table.
strategy.connector: Ofcom social tariffs page + CCW water company list

strategy.why: Travel costs, PPCs and exemption certificates sit next to the live health pack and reuse its facts.
Local crisis schemes, DHP and council grants differ in every council; this is the first step to thousands of schemes (one entry per council per service).
strategy.schemesEstimate: 317 English councils x several local schemes each (Scotland, Wales and NI to add)
strategy.connector: ONS council list + postcodes.io + council website reader

strategy.why: Charity grants for individuals are the largest pool of unclaimed help; 360Giving shows which funders actually pay individuals, and the regulators' registers fill in rules and areas.
strategy.schemesEstimate: Over 1,700 grant-giving organisations (Turn2us); 255,271 grants to individuals recorded in GrantNav
strategy.connector: 360Giving GrantNav + Charity Commission and OSCR downloads (Turn2us only with a licence)

strategy.why: Statutory pay, redundancy and insolvency claims are rights, not discretionary, and catch people at the moment of a life event.
